mica: quick heads-up  we've got a small but reproducible class of funcall parse failures on the zephyr-int4 canary. payload looks like valid JSON then ends with a few NUL or replacement chars. ~2.7% structured calls.

liam: sample capture: ```
{"tool":"kb_lookup","q":"serving guides"}��
```

jena: any strong correlates? batch size, kv cache, or seq len?

mica: yes: >80% when batch_size >= 10 AND kvcache=true. single-request flows are nearly clean.

pranav: sounds like a stray byte emission after token->string conversion in quant path. two-pronged plan: short-term postproc guard vs long-term runtime trace.

liam: propose 3 canary arms (flags only):
A) baseline
B) sanitizer: strip trailing non-utf8/NUL bytes, attempt NDJSON-last-object parse, + one retry
C) sentinel: append per-request random salted anchor `<<END:crc32:rand10>>` in postprompt and validate before parse

jena: metric plan: schema_compliance, parse_fallback_used, sanitizer_trim_pct, sentinel_collision_count, p95/p99 latency. 2k structured calls per arm should show signal.

pranav: add parse_error_class: invalid_utf8|trailing_nul|partial_json. also emit `postproc.arm` tag and kvcache_hit.

mica: infra follow-ups: dump post-decode token bytes for failed parses to secure bucket (PII-safe) and run a mirrored fp16 path for hex-diffing. filing INF-11011.

liam: implementation notes: keep both sanitizer and sentinel behind `postproc.sanitize_trail` and `postproc.sentinel_anchor` flags. sentinel should use per-request 10-byte random salt to make collisions negligible.

jena: if sanitizer heals but adds latency, gate it to only run on retry attempts to avoid p95 regressions. record `sanitizer_run_phase` (initial|retry).

canary-bot: canary update: zephyr-int4 at 5% traffic. rolling schema_fail_rate (30m): 2.7%.

mica: I'll run the 2k/arm eval overnight and post a short notebook with counts and latencies in this thread tomorrow AM. tagging prana and runtime team for root-cause. :mag:
